comment: Casting to a TV through Android's (Qualcomm) Wi-Fi Display stack: the root tool rungic-cast (shared/android/rungic-cast, /data/adb/rungic-wfd), run by the Rungic app for op cast on the platform bridge's socket ($RUNGIC_PLATFORM_SOCKET, one JSON object per line each way, one request per connection; a cast request may take a minute, connect three, resolution five and a half). The Linux consumer is desktop/cast/rungic-cast (used by the cast quick setting and rungic-cast-watch): it first asks the platform bridge's status (an app that does not answer is asleep: host-unreachable), then {op: cast, args: [command, argument]}. status and capabilities answer the same object: protocol_version 1 (the consumer refuses any other, or receivers that are not a list, as backend-incompatible), active_state (2: connected), active (the connected TV or null), reconnecting, receivers (one per TV) and displays; the quick setting reads active_state, active.name and reconnecting. Errors are {"error": string, "code": string}, code component-missing when the tool is not installed. scan, connect, disconnect, resolution and settings change what Android's Wi-Fi Display does or shows and are never sent by the provider check. Tested from both ends: tools/tests/test_contract_wifi_display.py (the real rungic-cast against tools/contracts.py's stand-in) and acceptance scenario contract.wifi-display (the app and the tool on the phone; TV names and addresses are blanked there).
